frontMatter.introduction: At Bedmutha Industries, we are dedicated to delivering high-performance engineering and manufacturing solutions with a focus on precision, safety, and sustainable growth. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual outlines the framework for standardized operations across our facilities. It serves as a reference for maintaining streamlined workflows, adhering to industry benchmarks, and ensuring every team member operates with clarity and purpose. This document reinforces our core philosophy—structured execution leads to consistent excellence.
frontMatter.objective:
This SOP Manual is developed with the following goals:

To provide a unified approach for operational procedures across all units.
To ensure strict adherence to national and international regulatory requirements.
To mitigate risks related to safety, quality, and operational disruptions.
To encourage a proactive and transparent work culture.

This manual is designed as a functional tool to support employees, supervisors, and stakeholders in aligning with Bedmutha Industries' principles. It also adapts to changes in regulations, technology, and market expectations, offering a flexible yet structured system for continuous growth and reliability.

Below are the key outcomes expected from SOP implementation:

Benefit Areas | Description
Operational Efficiency | Reduces Variability and streamlines Process.
Compliance Management | Ensures Alignment with Regulatory and legal standards.
Quality Assurance | Maintains Consistent Product and Service Quality.
Risk Mitigation | Lowers the likelihood of errors and workplace incidents.
Staff Empowerment | Equips employees with clear instructions and responsibilities.
frontMatter.scope: This manual applies to all internal staff, external vendors, service providers, and affiliated teams working across Bedmutha Industries' operations. It encompasses activities related to manufacturing, quality control, equipment handling, logistics, maintenance, and health & safety protocols. The SOP Manual is a living document and will be updated periodically to remain aligned with technological advancements and organizational objectives.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
To ensure this SOP remains relevant, up-to-date, and aligned with evolving business practices and regulatory requirements, Bedmutha Industries Limited has established an Annual SOP Manual Review Process, governed by the Compliance & IT Governance Teams.

Frequency:
This SOP is reviewed once every 12 months, or immediately after any critical breach, regulatory update, or major infrastructure change.

blocks.text: At Bedmutha Industries Limited, sustainability is not just a goal but a strategic business imperative. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines our integrated approach to improving energy efficiency, optimizing resource utilization, and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across all manufacturing and operational facilities. As a leading manufacturer of industrial wire products, we recognize our responsibility to mitigate environmental impact through proactive measures and sustainable innovations.
The primary objectives of this SOP are to:

Standardize procedures to enhance energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions.
Drive adoption of low-carbon technologies and operational best practices.
Comply with national and international environmental regulations.
Establish performance benchmarks and foster a culture of sustainability.

This SOP applies to all manufacturing units, warehouses, utilities, and administrative offices operated by Bedmutha Industries Limited. It is applicable to equipment operators, facility managers, engineering personnel, maintenance teams, procurement departments, and third-party contractors engaged in energy-related activities.

rows.definition: GHG is acronym for Greenhouse Gases. These are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming. Key GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and fluorinated gases.

CCS is acronym for Carbon Capture & Storage which is a technology designed to capture carbon dioxide emissions from industrial sources and store it underground to prevent it from entering the atmosphere.
CHP means Combined Heat & Power. It is a system that simultaneously generates usable heat and electricity from a single energy source, increasing overall efficiency.

VFD is acronym for Variable frequency Drive. It is an electronic device that controls the speed and torque of electric motors by varying input frequency and voltage, leading to significant energy savings.

body.text:
Conduct detailed energy monitoring to assess equipment performance.
Identify inefficient motors, compressors, HVAC systems, and lighting.
Replace outdated systems with high-efficiency models.
Optimize processes through automation and sensor integration.
Implement energy management software for real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance.
Benchmark results before and after equipment upgrades to validate efficiency gains.
Equipment Upgrade & Impact

Identify high-temperature exhaust systems (furnaces, boilers).
Install heat exchangers to capture waste heat.
Reuse captured heat for preheating feedwater or space heating.
Evaluate feasibility of CHP units for facilities with thermal + electrical load.
Monitor thermal efficiency post-installation using digital tools.

Flowchart: Waste Heat Recovery Process

[Heat Source] → [Heat Exchanger] → [Steam/Hot Air Generation] → [Use in Boilers or Cleaning Systems]
Benefits:

Reduces fuel consumption.
Lowers operational costs.
Minimizes thermal losses.
Improves system resilience and efficiency

Analyze current fuel usage patterns and carbon intensity.
Explore cleaner alternatives like PNG, biomass briquettes, and solar energy.
Replace diesel-based systems with hybrid or renewable-powered units.
Monitor emissions post-implementation using calibrated gas analyzers.
Collaborate with fuel suppliers for consistent supply of cleaner fuels.
Outcomes:

Significant reduction in direct CO2 emissions.
Strengthens compliance with long-term climate goals.

The selection of technology and equipment plays a crucial role in the success of energy and GHG management strategies. Bedmutha Industries follows a rigorous evaluation approach to ensure only the most effective and sustainable options are adopted.
Selection Considerations Include:

Energy Efficiency:
Preference is given to equipment with high energy performance ratings (e.g., IE3, IE4 motors, 5-star rated systems).
Evaluation of Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) benchmarks.
GHG Reduction Potential:
Focus on technologies with measurable impact on carbon emissions.
Preference for low-carbon alternatives such as electric vehicles and induction heating systems.
Certifications and Standards:
Equipment must meet or exceed ISO, BIS, CE, BEE, or equivalent standards.
Preference for vendors offering certified Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs).
Digital and Smart Integration:
Compatibility with SCADA, EMS, IoT sensors, and AI forecasting tools.
Support for cloud-based monitoring, automation, and performance tracking.
Reliability and Maintenance:
Preference for proven technologies with established track records.
Availability of local service centers and preventive maintenance plans.
Vendor Selection and Transparency:
Evaluation of vendor reputation, technical expertise, and sustainability practices.
Preference for vendors offering post-installation support, training, and documentation.
This structured selection process ensures that every investment contributes to long-term operational excellence and environmental sustainability.

responsibilities: Conduct periodic energy monitoring to identify areas of improvement.
Prepare and maintain detailed energy performance reports.
Recommend and support the implementation of efficiency improvement measures.
Approve capital investment for energy-saving technologies.
Allocate manpower and resources to sustainability initiatives.
Oversee the effectiveness of implemented measures and track progress.
Ensure timely maintenance of energy-related systems.
Calibrate instruments and systems for optimal energy performance.
Replace and upgrade inefficient components.
Ensure adherence to environmental regulations and GHG guidelines.
Document emission data and report discrepancies.
Conduct internal audits and safety inspections linked to energy systems.
Manage contracts with a focus on sustainability and energy performance.
Source high-efficiency and certified energy equipment.
Evaluate vendors based on environmental criteria.

blocks.text: To foster greater employee participation, the following initiatives have been introduced:

Awareness and Capacity Building
Training & Development: All new and existing employees undergo training sessions on energy-efficient practices, GHG reduction goals, and usage of smart systems.
Energy SOP Workshops: Special sessions are held annually to communicate changes or enhancements to the energy policy and SOP.
Onboarding Briefings: Sustainability and energy-saving guidelines are introduced during induction for all new recruits.
Participation Programs
Green Suggestion Box: Staff can submit practical ideas for energy savings. Winning suggestions are evaluated for pilot implementation.
Recognition and Motivation
Gamification and Rewards: Points-based systems encourage employees to take part in challenges like “Switch-Off Hours,” “Green Desk Week,” or “Low Carbon Commutes.” Winners receive certificates and recognition.
Sustainability Awards: Annual awards are presented to departments or individuals who significantly contribute to energy reduction efforts.
Engagement Platforms
Sustainability Day: A dedicated day each year to celebrate green milestones, share project outcomes, and encourage open dialogue on improvements.
Awareness Boards & Dashboards: Digital screens and noticeboards at plant locations display energy KPIs, live savings stats, and ongoing campaigns.
This SOP is reviewed:

Annually, or
After any regulatory change, or
If there is a change in equipment, process, or plant layout.

Water is a foundational element of industrial operations. At Bedmutha Industries Limited, we recognize our responsibility to manage water efficiently and sustainably. This SOP provides a holistic roadmap for conserving water, promoting reuse, and integrating modern water management techniques across all operations. The initiative supports regulatory compliance and aligns with our commitment to ISO 14001, Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) standards and long-term sustainability objectives.
The primary objectives of this SOP are to:

Optimize water use efficiency through modern technological interventions.
Strengthen recycling practices to reduce freshwater dependency.
Minimize water pollution by implementing effective wastewater management.
Encourage a culture of water conservation at all organizational levels.
Comply with national and international water regulations.

This SOP is applicable to all departments, plants, facilities, and external service providers of Bedmutha Industries Limited that utilize water in their operations. It includes production lines, utilities, sanitation, HVAC systems, landscaping, and administrative areas.

rows.definition: Treated process water reused for secondary applications like cooling and cleaning.
Collecting and storing rooftop rainwater for internal non-potable use.
Lightly contaminated water from wash basins, cleaning, and rinsing that can be treated and reused.
A cooling system that recirculates the same water, reducing fresh water intake.
Rapid cooling of metal products using water to increase hardness.
Process to remove sharp edges or burrs from metal parts, often using water jets or slurry-based systems.

body.text:
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP): Designed to treat and detoxify industrial effluent before reuse or discharge.
Reverse Osmosis (RO): Removes dissolved solids, ideal for reusing rinse and greywater.
Membrane Bioreactor (MBR): Combines biological treatment and membrane filtration for high-quality treated water.
Reuse Applications
Efficient cooling mechanisms reduce water wastage and operating costs.

Closed-loop systems recirculate cooling water to reduce evaporation losses.
Air-cooled chillers are deployed where humidity and ambient conditions permit.
Automated controls (float valves, timers) prevent overflow and leaks.

Flowchart: Closed-Loop Cooling Water Flow

[Chiller Unit] → [Distribution Line] → [Cooling Process] → [Return Pipe] → [Holding Tank] → [Reused]
Surface preparation and cleaning processes are optimized by:

Implementing dry methods like air jet cleaning before water-based cleaning.
Using low-toxicity, biodegradable degreasers that need fewer rinse cycles.
Installing nozzles with flow restrictors to maintain pressure with less water.
Checklist for Opeartors:

Dry cleaning applied before rinsing.
Eco-friendly degreasing chemical used.
Final rinse water sourced from greywater treatment.
Rainwater is an excellent alternative to reduce dependence on groundwater.

Collection from rooftop gutters into storage tanks.
First flush systems prevent entry of dirt and debris.
Filtered water is used for toilets, landscaping, or sent to ETP for processing.

Illustration: Rainwater Harvesting Process

[Roof] → [Gutter] → [First Flush System] → [Storage Tank] → [Filtration] → [Non-potable Use]

steps.heading: Control of Wastewater from Finishing Operations

body.text: Finishing activities like quenching and deburring produce water waste that must be treated.

Oil-water separators extract oils from quenching fluids.
Settling tanks allow removal of metallic particulates from deburring wastewater.
Reclaimed water is recycled after treatment for reuse in compatible processes.

The selection of water conservation technologies and equipment is pivotal to the success of sustainable water management strategies. Bedmutha Industries adopts a structured and performance-driven evaluation process to ensure the integration of solutions that maximize reuse, minimize consumption, and align with long-term environmental goals.

Water Efficiency: Preference for systems with lower L/unit ratings.
Ease of Maintenance: Availability of spares and technical support.
Lifecycle Cost: CAPEX vs OPEX for optimal ROI.
Environmental Compliance: Conformity with CGWA and CPCB norms.
Smart Integration: IoT-enabled devices for monitoring and automation.

responsibilities: Monitor water consumption trends and identify inefficiencies.
Coordinate implementation of reuse and recycling strategies
Maintain documentation for audits and ensure regulatory compliance.
Inspect and maintain plumbing systems to prevent leakages.
Operate and service water treatment and recycling units.
Ensure automation systems (sensors, valves) are functional and calibrated
Conduct awareness programs on water conservation.
Carry out internal water audits and inspections.
Recommend technical upgrades based on performance gaps.
Source water-efficient fixtures and technologies.
Evaluate vendor performance based on water management criteria.
Ensure environmental compliance of outsourced services

blocks.text: To foster greater employee participation, the following initiatives have been introduced:

Awareness and Empowerment Initiatives

Immersive Training Modules: Mandatory training sessions are conducted for all employees to build awareness on water conservation goals, efficient cleaning practices, and appropriate responses to leakages or water-related incidents.
Interactive SOP Briefings: Annually workshops are organized to familiarize teams with updates to the Water Management SOP, introduce new technologies like rainwater harvesting systems and filtration units, and address on-ground implementation challenges.

Air pollution is one of the most critical environmental challenges faced by the manufacturing sector. At Bedmutha Industries Limited, we are committed to minimizing air pollutant emissions and ensuring compliance with national and international environmental regulations. This SOP outlines our approach to controlling, monitoring, and reducing air pollution from our operations.

To establish a systematic approach for preventing and controlling air pollution.
To ensure compliance with the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, CPCB guidelines, and MoEF&CC standards.
To implement best practices and innovative technologies to reduce emissions.
To safeguard the health of employees and surrounding communities.

rows.definition: Microscopic solid or liquid particles suspended in air, such as dust, dirt, soot, or smoke.
Volatile Organic Compounds are organic chemicals that easily become vapors or gases. Common in solvents, paints, and fuels.
Nitrogen Oxides (NOₓ) and Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) are combustion-related gases that contribute to smog and acid rain.
ESP is acronym for Electrostatic Precipitator which is an equipment that uses electrical charge to remove fine particles from gas streams.
Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems are automated systems that monitor pollutant levels in stack emissions.
Emissions not released through a stack or vent, such as dust from handling materials or leaks from equipment.
A pollution control technique using living material to capture and biologically degrade pollutants.
The assessment of outdoor air quality by measuring key pollutants at fixed locations over time.

responsibilities: SOP implementation, monitoring & compliance
Ensure upkeep of pollution control devices
Execution of preventive measures
Source eco-friendly equipment and materials
Report leaks, damages, or nuisances

substeps.text: Installation of Bag Filters: Captures fine particulate matter from furnaces and grinding operations.
Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP): Used in large-scale furnaces to remove PM from flue gases.
Wet Scrubbers: Installed for acid gas neutralization (SO₂, HCl).
Low-NOx Burners: Installed in boilers to reduce NOx formation during combustion.
Water Sprinkling Systems: Regular sprinkling on roads and raw material stockyards.
Enclosed Conveyors: Material handling systems are enclosed to prevent dust escape.
Dust Extraction Systems: Provided at key locations like bagging and grinding units.

This SOP provides a comprehensive framework for the management of materials and chemicals used in Bedmutha Industries’ operations. It ensures safe handling, storage, usage, and disposal of raw materials, hazardous substances, and chemicals, in compliance with environmental and safety standards. This includes sustainable practices like material consumption reduction, eco-friendly substitutions, and hazardous substance minimization.

This SOP applies to all plant facilities, operational departments, warehouses, laboratories, and logistics chains at Bedmutha Industries involved in procurement, transport, storage, processing, and disposal of materials and chemicals.

rows.definition: Substances that pose a risk to health, safety, or environment due to flammability, toxicity, or reactivity.
Material Safety Data Sheet, a document outlining safety, health, and environmental hazards associated with chemicals.
Persistent Organic Pollutants that resist degradation and accumulate in ecosystems.
Design of chemical products/processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
Strategies to reduce material and energy use while improving output.

body.text: Objective: Optimize processes to minimize the raw material input required per unit of production.
Measures:

Lean Manufacturing principles integrated in production lines.
Material flow analysis using digital twin simulations.
Real-time monitoring of raw material consumption via ERP.
Flowchart: Material Optimization Loop

Use of biodegradable coolants and cutting fluids in machining.
Replacement of solvent-based degreasers with water-based variants.
Preference to suppliers offering REACH and RoHS certified chemicals.
Acid Rinse Recovery System : Closed-loop reuse of phosphating rinse water reducing chemical load by 80%

Corrosion-resistant racks and leak-proof containers.
Temperature-controlled storage for flammable liquids.
Color-coded segregation: Red (Flammable), Yellow (Reactive), Blue (Corrosive)
GHS-compliant labels with pictograms, hazard codes, and first aid.

Use of certified containers with spill-proof lids.
Transport documents include MSDS and emergency response guide.

Neutralization Units: On-site units treat acidic and basic waste.
Incineration: For non-recyclable toxic materials via authorized third parties.
Heavy Metal Capture: Effluent treatment plant uses chelating agents.

Substitution of lead-based solder with tin-silver alloys.
Low-VOC paints and coatings in manufacturing.
Inert atmosphere in chemical processing to reduce secondary emissions.

Old: Lead Solder (for PCB Assembly)

New: Tin-Silver Alloy → Reduction: 100%

Old: VOC Paint (for coating processes)

New: Water-Based Paint → Reduction: 92%
Actions to Eliminate Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)

No use of POPs listed under Stockholm Convention.
Product and raw material screening to detect POP traces.
Audit suppliers for POP-free certification.

narrative.text:
Digital inventory tools track chemical inflow/outflow.
QR-coded containers for traceability.
Bi-annual third-party chemical management audits.

blocks.text:
Feedback loop from floor operators to R&D.
Annual revision of SOP based on audit results.
Benchmarking against global metal industry leaders.
This SOP is reviewed:

Annually, or
After any regulatory change, or
If there is a change in equipment, process, or plant layout.

To establish a structured waste management system that ensures minimization, proper segregation, safe handling, recycling, and disposal of waste at Bedmutha Industries. The SOP also aligns with sustainability goals and compliance with environmental regulations.
Applicable across all operational departments, manufacturing units, warehouses, and administrative buildings of Bedmutha Industries where waste is generated, handled, or disposed.

rows.definition: Categories of waste generated during operations – solid, liquid, hazardous, recyclable, organic, etc.
Extended Producer Responsibility.
The separation of waste into predefined categories at the source.

rows: Reused or sold to scrap dealers

responsibilities: Overall compliance, audits, and reporting
Implementation at unit level, reporting deviations
Proper segregation, following disposal practices
Collection, transport, and processing as per norms

body.text: Bedmutha Industries is committed to minimizing internal waste generation through the principles of source reduction, reuse, and resource recovery. These measures are integrated into operational workflows to promote a circular approach.
Key Strategies:

Process Optimization: Use of Lean Manufacturing tools (e.g., Kaizen, 5S) to reduce raw material wastage during production.
Material Reuse: Return of offcuts, defective items, and packaging back into the production line where feasible.
Byproduct Recovery:

Metal scrap from wire manufacturing is collected and remelted.
Sludge from electroplating units is filtered and stored for recycling via authorized vendors.
Packaging Minimization: Replacing multi-layer packaging with recyclable mono-material alternatives.

rows: Repaired and reused for next shipments

blocks.text: Waste Streams:

rows: Waste with flammable, toxic, reactive, or corrosive properties
Used machine oil, spent acid, contaminated rags, degreasing solvents
Waste not posing direct health/environmental risk
Paper, cardboard, plastic packaging, rejected product parts
Organic material from canteens or landscaping
Food scraps, tea waste, garden trimmings
Copper offcuts, rejected wires, aluminum trimmings

blocks.text: Sorting and Disposal Steps:

body.text:
Color-coded bins are placed at generation points (e.g., production floor, offices, canteen)
Labels include waste type and disposal instructions
Examples:
🟥 Red bin – for hazardous waste like used oil containers
🟩 Green bin – for organic canteen waste
🟦 Blue bin – for paper and recyclable plastics

Each shift supervisor logs waste quantity at the end of shift
Example: 35 kg of copper scrap, 2 drums of spent acid.

Hazardous waste is stored in secondary containment tanks or spill-proof containers
Non-hazardous materials are sorted in designated storage zones
Example: Flammable liquids stored in ventilated, explosion-proof cabinets

Hazardous Waste → Sent to TSDF via authorized transporters with Form 10 manifest
Scrap Metal → Collected and sent to approved recyclers
E-Waste → Handover to CPCB-authorized e-waste handlers
Canteen Waste → Sent to in-house bio-compost unit or municipal disposal service
Bedmutha Industries has established a robust waste traceability framework to ensure end-to-end tracking of waste from generation to final disposal.

Tracking Mechanism: A digital tracking system using barcode and RFID tagging is implemented for key waste streams such as metal scrap, lubricants, chemical containers, and packaging waste.
Waste Mapping: Each generation point (e.g., wire drawing units, ETP, packaging stations) is mapped with corresponding waste streams, assigned unique IDs for traceability.
Certified Partners: All disposal and recycling are carried out via authorized waste management partners, registered with the Pollution Control Boards (SPCB/CPCB).
Documentation: Movement of hazardous waste is recorded using Form 10 manifests under the Hazardous Waste Management Rules, 2016.

narrative.text:
Monthly Reports: Waste movement, treatment, and disposal data are compiled into internal reports using ERP-based waste management software.
Compliance Checks: Regular checks ensure that disposal aligns with SPCB/CPCB protocols.
Audit Trail: A full audit trail is maintained for high-risk wastes (e.g., ETP sludge, used oils) including date, handler, vehicle details, and receiving party acknowledgments.

blocks.text:
Certified Disposal Vendors: Only licensed recyclers, TSDF facilities, and hazardous waste handlers are partnered with for final disposal.
Categorized Disposal: Waste is sorted into categories—hazardous, recyclable, biodegradable, and general industrial waste—and treated accordingly.
Storage Protocols: Temporary waste storage is done in designated, labeled, and ventilated enclosures to prevent spills, contamination, or unauthorized access.

Frequency: Conduct annual reviews or upon any process/materials change
Review Team: Includes Waste Management Team, Environmental Compliance Lead, and Operations Head

This SOP defines the policies, procedures, and guidelines for ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of all employees at Bedmutha Industries Limited. It aims to prevent workplace injuries and illnesses through proactive planning, risk assessment, employee training, and wellness initiatives, while ensuring full compliance with legal and regulatory frameworks.

Applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party personnel operating at or visiting Bedmutha Industries’ facilities, including administrative offices, manufacturing units, workshops, warehouses, and logistics areas.

rows.definition: Environment, Health, and Safety
Personal Protective Equipment
Repetitive Strain Injury
Material Safety Data Sheet
Occupational Safety and Health
Time-Weighted Average for exposure limits to noise or substances
Lockout-Tagout – energy isolation safety system

responsibilities: Policy implementation, risk assessments, and audits
Oversee daily compliance and training enforcement
Conduct toolbox talks, monitor practices, report incidents
Adhere to all safety procedures, wear PPE, report hazards

blocks.text: Bedmutha Industries is committed to ensuring all work areas are designed, operated, and maintained in ways that reduce risk and enhance employee well-being.

substeps.text: Slip-resistant flooring and sufficient lighting throughout the facility
Guardrails at elevated work zones, secured platforms for maintenance
Fire safety systems including ABC extinguishers, alarms, and clearly marked evacuation routes
Regular inspection and maintenance of safety-critical infrastructure.
Proper aisle marking, lighting, and emergency signage throughout the plant.

steps.heading: Chemical and Hazardous Substance Exposure Control

substeps.text: MSDS available at every chemical storage or use point
Use of sealed containers, spillage trays, and chemical-resistant PPE
Local fume extractors and general ventilation systems
Substitution of hazardous materials with low-toxicity or water-based alternatives where feasible
Real-time exposure monitoring in designated hazard zones
Noise mapping conducted for all high-noise operations
Areas above 85 dB(A) marked as “Hearing Protection Zones”
Use of earplugs or earmuffs is mandatory in these zones
Acoustic enclosures installed on generators, blowers, and compressors
Vibration dampeners and proper equipment maintenance reduce secondary sound hazards
Ergonomic tools and adjustable workstations installed at high-risk areas.
Anti-fatigue mats provided for prolonged standing operations.
Job rotation and micro-breaks implemented to reduce repetitive motion strain.
Posture awareness visuals and RSI prevention guidance displayed at workstations.
RSI cases tracked and reviewed for early intervention.
Annual health check-ups including vision, hearing, and respiratory tests.
Tie-ups with local hospitals for emergency care.
Onsite medical room with first-aid trained personnel.
Weekly yoga and mental wellness programs.
Nutrition counseling and clean drinking water stations.

blocks.text: Flowchart: Emergency Response Protocol

substeps.text: Fire evacuation drills every 6 months.
Emergency Response Team (ERT) in each department.
Clearly marked muster points and evacuation maps.
Training on CPR, first aid, and fire extinguisher use.

narrative.text:
Daily safety inspections by line supervisors.
Monthly internal audits using standardized checklists.
Non-compliance is escalated to the Operations Head.
Integration with ISO 45001:2018 for occupational health & safety management.

blocks.text:
This SOP is reviewed annually or post any major incident.
Review board includes EHS Head, Operations Manager, and an external safety consultant.
Employee feedback is used for continual refinement.

The purpose of this SOP is to establish a robust and structured system for career management and training to support employee growth, increase job satisfaction, and ensure the strategic development of skills aligned with the business goals of Bedmutha Industries Ltd. The SOP outlines the processes to identify employee potential, build competencies, and provide opportunities for career advancement while fostering a culture of continuous learning.

All full-time and part-time employees at all hierarchical levels.
All departments and functional areas across Bedmutha's manufacturing and corporate units.
All stages of employment, from onboarding to leadership roles.

To systematically develop and upgrade employee skills.
To align individual goals with organizational growth and performance.
To identify and nurture high-potential talent for future leadership roles.
To create structured career paths and individual development plans (IDPs).
To ensure employees are equipped with current and future-ready competencies.

This SOP outlines Bedmutha Industries Ltd.'s commitment to operating with integrity, transparency, and in compliance with anti-corruption laws. It defines procedures and responsibilities to prevent, detect, and respond to any form of corruption, bribery, or unethical behavior in our business operations.
This policy is applicable to:

All employees, including full-time, part-time, contract, and temporary staff.
Members of the Board of Directors and executive management.
External stakeholders such as contractors, vendors, agents, consultants, and third-party intermediaries representing the company in any capacity.

rows.definition: Offering, promising, giving, accepting, or soliciting an undue advantage or anything of value with the intent to influence the actions of a person in a position of trust.
Abuse of entrusted power for private gain, including bribery, embezzlement, kickbacks, favoritism, and nepotism.
Small, unofficial payments made to expedite routine actions by officials. These are considered illegal and are strictly prohibited.
The return of a portion of money received, often secretly or illegally, in exchange for favorable treatment.

responsibilities: Must comply with all anti-corruption policies and laws.
Must report any suspected instances of corruption or unethical behavior.
Must not accept or offer bribes in any form.
Must set an example of ethical conduct.
Must ensure employees under their supervision understand and follow this SOP.
Must support investigations into policy breaches.
Responsible for policy implementation, updates, and training.
Investigates all reported incidents and recommends action.
Maintains logs of complaints, investigations, and actions taken.
Must sign an agreement to follow this policy before commencing any work.
Must not engage in any corrupt practices while working with the company.
Subject to audits and monitoring for compliance.

body.text:
Permissible only if:
Of nominal value.
Given transparently and occasionally.
Not intended to influence business decisions.
Not permissible if:
Given in exchange for favorable treatment.
Excessive, frequent, or in the form of cash/gift cards.
Undocumented or intended to bypass company policies.

rows: Any gift above ₹5,000 in value (per instance or cumulative in one calendar year) is not permitted. Gifts below this value may be accepted only with prior written approval from HR.
Occasional business meals are acceptable if under ₹2,000 per person and not frequent. Lavish entertainment, personal trips, or expensive event tickets are prohibited.
Accepting personal favors, travel, or sponsorship from vendors under consideration for contracts is strictly prohibited, regardless of value.
Example: An employee working in procurement must disclose if a family member owns or works in a supplier company — even if that company is not currently active.
Cash gifts, vouchers, or gift cards of any amount are not allowed. Even festive vouchers are treated as improper unless issued officially by the company.

body.text:
No bribes, unofficial payments, or gifts may be offered to officials.
All interactions with officials must be recorded and approved by senior management.

Must be transparent, legal, and approved by senior management.
Cannot be used as a cover for bribery or to gain any improper advantage.

Before engaging a vendor/agent, Bedmutha perform due diligence to verify their integrity.
Anti-corruption clauses must be included in all third-party agreements.
Periodic monitoring and audits are mandatory.

All financial transactions must be recorded accurately and transparently.
No use of off-the-books accounts or falsified records.
All expenses, including gifts and hospitality, must be properly documented and approved.

steps.heading: Handling Transactions - Step 1: Initiation of Transaction

body.text:
A transaction request must be initiated by an authorized employee.
For purchases, a Purchase Requisition (PR) must be submitted via the internal procurement system, citing proper justification and budget approval.

The transaction go through multi-level approval:
Department Head approval
Budgetary control check
Finance Department vetting

Perform due diligence for all third parties involved:
Legal identity verification
Background checks for corruption or fraud history
Signed declaration of compliance with the Anti-Corruption SOP
Ensure the vendor/client is onboarded in the official ERP system.

Work only proceeds after formal approval and documentation.
Monitor progress, delivery, and billing based on agreed milestones.

All payments must be:
Matched against purchase orders, invoices, and delivery receipts
Reviewed and verified by Accounts Payable and Finance
Made through traceable banking channels—no cash transactions

Maintain digital and physical copies of:
Invoices
Contracts
Approvals
Audit trails
Records are stored securely for at least 7 years for audit purposes.

Finance and Internal Audit teams conduct random transaction audits annually.
Any red flags or irregularities are reported immediately to the Compliance Officer.

Violations of this SOP result in:
Disciplinary actions up to and including dismissal.
Termination of business relationships with vendors/agents.
Legal reporting to enforcement authorities.
Financial penalties or reputational consequences.

narrative.text:
Internal audits are conducted at least once a year.
Surprise audits and forensic reviews are done in high-risk areas.
External audits are conducted by third parties when necessary.
All audit findings are reviewed by the Audit Committee and senior management.

blocks.text: This SOP is reviewed annually or when:

There are operational changes in business processes.
Audit findings or incidents require policy revision.
Amendments are communicated to all stakeholders via emails, meetings.

sops.title: Incident Response Plan (IRP) – Confidential Information Breaches

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedure for detecting, reporting, responding to, and mitigating any breach or unauthorized access involving confidential information, including employee data, customer records, financial details, and proprietary operational data. The plan ensures quick containment and minimal impact, while protecting the interests of Bedmutha Industries Ltd and its stakeholders.
Applies to all departments, locations, systems, and personnel (internal or external) who handle or access confidential and sensitive information, including:

Employee records
Customer/vendor data
Financial and legal information
Proprietary process, product, or R&D information
Network/system security credentials

rows.definition: Any non-public information that can impact privacy, operations, or compliance
An attempted or successful unauthorized access, disclosure, or misuse of information
A confirmed event in which confidential information is lost, stolen, or exposed

responsibilities: Coordinates IRP activation, investigation, and technical response
Ensures regulatory reporting, legal review, and records of actions taken
Supports internal communication and corrective actions
Identifies impact of breach and supports recovery

body.text:
All employees must report suspicious activity or confirmed breach within 1 hour
Notification to: incident@bedmutha.com
Examples: unusual login alerts, unauthorized data transfer, lost devices, phishing attack

IT isolates affected system/network/device
Access rights are revoked, and firewalls updated
Any malware is removed and logs are captured for evidence

Identify type of data compromised (PII, business confidential, customer data)
Evaluate scope: number of records, systems affected, potential harm

Notify: Affected internal stakeholders (via email/memo); Regulatory bodies (if required by law – e.g., under IT Act or GDPR-like clauses); Customers/vendors (if relevant and under guidance of legal team)
Communication is approved by the Director – Information Security & Compliance Officer

Restore systems from clean backups
Change access credentials across affected endpoints
Monitor post-incident for anomalies

Root cause analysis performed by IT + Compliance within 3 working days
Report includes: Timeline of incident; Actions taken; Weaknesses exploited; Corrective actions

Internal debrief session conducted within 7 days
Lessons learned are applied to update this SOP, training programs, or IT policy

blocks.text:
Quarterly employee training on data handling, phishing awareness, and reporting channels
Access to confidential data is based on job role (least privilege principle)
All USBs and external media are restricted
MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) is enabled across all cloud and email systems
All incident reports are logged in the Information Security Incident Register and include:

Incident ID
Time of detection
Reported by
Systems affected
Type of data breached
Actions taken
Communication details
Lessons learned
Retention period: 7 years

This IRP SOP is reviewed annually or following any major breach
Post-incident analysis directly informs: Firewall rule updates; Access control adjustments

The purpose of this SOP is to define the principles and procedures for managing information in a secure, ethical, and legally compliant manner. Information is a vital asset that, if mishandled, can lead to data breaches, financial loss, reputational damage, and legal implications.
This SOP applies to all employees, vendors, contractors, consultants, and temporary workers who handle company data.

rows.definition: Non-public data including business strategies, employee records, customer/vendor information, R&D data, etc.
Any information related to an identified or identifiable individual.
Unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of information.

body.text: To manage data effectively, Bedmutha Industries classifies data into four primary categories.

rows: Financial reports, HR files, legal notices

body.text: A. Physical Records

Use lockable cabinets.
Limit key/card access to authorized personnel.
Avoid storing important records near areas with fire or water risk.
B. Digital Records

Use encrypted servers and secure cloud services.
Backup critical systems daily, store backups offsite or on a secure cloud.
Use anti-virus software and firewalls to prevent unauthorized access.
Access Control

Implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and employees can only access what they need.
Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for sensitive systems.
Regularly review and update access privileges, especially after role changes or exits.
Use audit logs to track who accessed what data and when.
Data Sharing & Transfer Protocols
Internal Sharing:

Use approved platforms.
Use read-only files where edits are not needed.
External Sharing:

Sign NDAs before sharing sensitive data with clients.
Transfer files through encrypted links or VPN.
Do not send business data through personal emails or apps.
Data Retention
Each type of data must be retained for a specified time as per compliance.
Secure Disposal Methods
Paper Records:

Shred documents using cross-cut shredders.
Keep shredding logs.
Digital Files:

Use data-wiping software to erase content.
Ensure old laptops are degaussed or destroyed before disposal.
Disposal Authorization:

Must be approved by data owner + Compliance Officer.
Maintain a Disposal Register for tracking.
Continuous Audits and Monitoring

blocks.text:
Reviewed annually or when new data laws are introduced.
Changes are reviewed by IT, Legal, and Compliance team.

sops.title: Internal Audits of Ethics & Compliance Control Procedures

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the methodology for conducting internal audits to evaluate the effectiveness of Bedmutha Industries’ ethics and compliance control systems. These audits are designed to detect potential gaps, ensure continuous improvement, and support legal compliance and ethical conduct across all functions and third-party relationships.
Audits are conducted to assess the following key areas

Procurement and supply chain integrity
Anti-bribery and corruption policy implementation
Employee awareness and ethics training
Regulatory compliance with national and global anti-corruption laws
Whistleblower mechanism and non-retaliation practices
Financial transparency and fraud controls
Third-party risk management and screening
Information security controls and data protection measures

body.text: The audit uses a structured questionnaire-based assessment aligned with your Internal Assessment Form. This includes:

15+ key control questions to be answered as Yes / No
Document review and system walkthroughs
Interviews with department heads and key employees
Sample testing of procurement decisions, training records, financial entries, and whistleblower logs
Retrospective review of ethics policy effectiveness and compliance incidents
Employees involved in the audit must sign an undertaking confirming accurate disclosure.

blocks.text:
All completed forms, audit reports, and follow-up logs are stored in the Compliance Shared Drive
Copies of final assessments are signed and acknowledged by Management
Retention period: 7 years in line with audit and legal policy

narrative.text:
Findings are categorized as: Observations, Minor Non-conformities, or Major Non-conformities
A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) must be developed within 15 days for each finding
High-risk or repeated issues are escalated to the Ethics Committee and Board Compliance Officer
Follow-up is conducted within 30 to 60 days to verify closure

blocks.text:
The Internal Assessment Form and audit checklist are updated annually
Compliance team reviews trends from past audit cycles to inform training and policy updates
Adjustments are made to improve scope, frequency, or accountability mechanisms
